data.title: BankThink The fintech graveyard is full of companies that grew too fast
data.description:
• Key insight: It’s extremely difficult to scale fraud controls at the same rate as customer growth. But the fintechs that fail to do it are leaving themselves vulnerable to the kind of attacks that can prove fatal to a young company.
  • Forward look: The future belongs to fintech firms that make sure to develop their fraud controls alongside their growth.

When fintech founders craft their pitch decks, they invariably include charts with lines soaring from the bottom left to the top right. Those charts can be about almost anything — revenue, customers, transactions, volumes.

data.title: BankThink A sovereign debt crisis in the US would quickly go global
data.description:
• Key insight: Amid high inflation, a soaring national debt and geopolitical uncertainty, a serious threat to the stability of U.S. Treasury markets is a real danger. A U.S. bond rout would have devastating worldwide consequences.
  • Supporting data: Federal debt recently hit 100% of U.S. GDP, the latest annual budget showed a$2 trillion gap, and there is talk that America will hit its debt ceiling, some $41.1 trillion, in the first half of next year.

Geopolitical uncertainty, high inflation, and elevated interest rates have tested every major economy this year, but amid a global bond sell-off, a new and potentially even more damaging scenario is on the horizon: a sustained bond rout in the U.S. Treasury market.

data.title: Can credit cards still be profitable if rates are capped? Yes
data.description:
• Supporting data: Borrowers with FICO scores of 600 generate over 10% ROA for issuers, compared with just over 5% for those with scores of 850, according to New York Federal Reserve researchers.
  • Expert Quote: “I’m sympathetic to concerns about reducing access to credit. This was why I wrote the report … I think a 10% cap would reduce access by a very small amount, and a slightly higher rate cap would not reduce lending at all.” —Vanderbilt researcher Brian Shearer

Credit card issuers have ample cushion to adapt to a 10% cap on interest rates without drastically reducing credit access for consumers and the measure would save consumers billions, should such a limit be imposed by lawmakers.

data.title: Payoneer gets conditional OCC approval for stablecoin bank
data.description:

International payments company Payoneer has received conditional approval from U.S. federal regulators to establish PAYO Digital Bank, a trust bank built for stablecoins.

data.title: What FinCEN’s intrusion means for banks’ SAR filings
data.description:
• Key insight: FinCEN’s batch-filing channel was down by Nov. 19, and one compliance vendor could not file through FinCEN’s website from Nov. 21 until as late as Tuesday, when the bureau disclosed unauthorized access to some of its systems.
  • What’s at stake: Suspicious activity reports are confidential by law and can name people a bank suspects of wrongdoing. There is no evidence so far that the database holding them was breached, a source close to the matter said.

data.title: BankThink Playing your greatest hits isn’t always what the audience wants
data.description:
• Key insight: Banks build their brands on trust, stability and service. But it pays to remember that customers evolve, and that the kind of banking relationships your oldest account holders value might not match what their kids prefer.

I sometimes find myself thinking about business practices in the most unusual places.

data.title: Fed’s Bowman says decisive action key to supervision modernization
data.description:
• Key insight: Federal Reserve Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman urged bank regulators in Latin America to focus on material risks and empower their examiners to take decisive action when issues are identified.
  • Expert quote: “The ultimate measure of successful and effective supervision is the ability to recognize material risks and act effectively while there is still time to influence the outcome.” — Federal Reserve Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman

The Federal Reserve’s top regulator continued her campaign to urge international bank supervisors to follow her lead in focusing on material financial risks.

data.title: Inside the fight to define what perpetual futures really are
data.description:
• Key insight: Two lawsuits are challenging the Commodity Futures Trading Commission’s classification of crypto and single-stock perpetual futures as futures rather than swaps, which carry more stringent regulatory and compliance requirements. 
  • Expert quote: “Success will protect these new market entrants more than or as much as legislation would.” — Peter Curley, head of global regulatory affairs at blockchain-based financial technology company Ondo Finance

WASHINGTON — Crypto and single-stock perpetual futures are now trading on some U.S. exchanges, but legal challenges to what perpetual futures really are may complicate the market for the novel contracts.
